details:
SDK version: 3.10.1

Client up to date as of 1/16/26

Issue:  There is a networked object with OnOwnershipRequest() and a UdonSynced value.    When a player "takes ownership" of the object, they will attempt to set ownership to themselves (if not already the owner) and change the UdonSynced value.  OnOwnershipRequest returns false if the UdonSynced value is not at its default.   When an owner and a non-owner simultaneously try to "take ownership," both will change the UdonSynced value locally and third parties will correctly receive the correct new value, the non-owner will fail to ever receive the owner's correct value, even if it is different from their own locally set value.

Reproduction:

1) Create an empty scene

2) Create a cube and attach the included script to it

3) "Build & Test You World" with 2 clients

4) Interact with the cube once with one of the two clients.

   

The attached script will use server time to make both clients simultaneously in real time attempt to take ownership of the object and change its UdonSynced int value to the local player's playerId.  The script also attempts to use OnOwnershipRequest to prevent ownership transfer when the UdonSynced int has been changed and is not at its default value.  After 5 seconds the script will log the local UdonSynced int value and then reset the value.

Expected behavior: Ownership should not transfer, the non-owner should receive a OnDeserialization() changing the value of the UdonSynced int to "1", and the local UdonSynced int value logged before the reset should be "1" on both clients.

Actual behavior: Ownership is transferred to the owner despite never losing ownership,  the non-owner never receives the OnDeserialization() changing the value of the UdonSynced int to "1, and the local UdonSynced int value logged before the reset is "1" for the owner, but "2" for the non-owner.

Workaround: Since this triggers OnOwnershipTransferred() on the owner's client, putting an additional RequestSerialization() here will force the value to be resent to the non-owner, ideally working the second time.

Additional observations:

Ownership DOES correctly sync from what I have observed

If you "Build & Test You World" with 3 clients, sync will work as expected.  But the original owner of the object will lose ownership despite rejecting all ownership transfer requests.

if you "Build & Test You World" with 3 clients but make it so only the owner and 1 non-owner perform the above test, the problem will be replicated but the second non-owner will correctly receive the sync value from the owner.
title: OnOwnershipRequest causes simultaneous attempts to set a network value to break between an owner and non-owner
